result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent the diff changes the fallback to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but this branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the find predicate can never match and the fallback always yields undefined — the previous fallback to `destinationCalendar.externalId` is gone (same broken pattern in updateEvent). Deletions/updates without an explicit externalCalendarId now get no calendar id.

judged_text: The Google Calendar deletion code searches for a missing externalCalendarId instead of falling back to a configured destination, breaking the destination fallback for deletions.

record.issue_text: The Google Calendar deletion code searches for a missing externalCalendarId instead of falling back to a configured destination, breaking the destination fallback for deletions.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in GoogleCalendarService.ts for deleteEvent (lines 312-316), the code changes from `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` to `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. This is logically flawed - when externalCalendarId is falsy (the else branch), it searches for a calendar where externalId equals the falsy externalCalendarId, which will never find anything meaningful. The same bug appears in updateEvent (line 253). This breaks the fallback behavior that should use the destination calendar when no externalCalendarId is provided.
